title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows an impersonation fraud enabled by AI-generated video and deepfakes. Scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles featuring AI-generated videos of a real immigration attorney offering fraudulent services, directing victims to contact numbers where they were solicited for payments. The fraud targeted a vulnerable population seeking immigration assistance.

The deployment failure occurred entirely on the scammers' side, not in the attorney's systems. Social media platforms hosted the fake accounts and videos without catching that they impersonated a real person offering services. It would have taken identity verification of account holders and detection of deepfake or AI-generated video content to prevent the accounts from being created or widely distributed.

It is not established who created the scam, how they obtained or created the video material, or what technical methods were used to generate it. The incident demonstrates that AI video generation tools can be used for fraud, but does not establish the scope of the technical capability or the identity of those responsible.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos depicting Leal offering fraudulent immigration services, including US residency assistance for $2,200. The scams escalated dramatically over the past three months after potential clients began calling his office. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram.

The fraudulent scheme typically begins with social media videos directing immigrants to contact a WhatsApp number, where scammers send fake contracts and payment requests through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Some fake videos feature testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal for obtaining their legal status. Leal warns immigrants to be cautious of online legal service advertisements and to verify identities before paying. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scam's origin.
